Eagan, Minnesota → Ann Arbor, Michigan

Nirav Singhal

Investing Journey

What pulls me toward markets is telling a company's story through its numbers. Last summer I traced referral volume at a medical device company through orders and shipments to build a top-line estimate for shareholders, and as Industrials Sector Head I had a week to learn an FCFE yield valuation, explain it to my team, and defend it in front of the club. Breaking a business down into its unit economics under a deadline, then using that to argue what it's actually worth, is what got me into this in the first place.

First Trade

In June 2022, my dad let me pick a stock for his portfolio. I had no real thesis, so I eeny-meeny-miny-mo'ed my way to $ENPH at $184.

$ENPH, Jun 2022–Dec 2023 · actual closing prices

By September it had run to $318, up 73% in three months. I felt like I'd cracked the code. It kept climbing without me into a new all-time high near $336 that December. Then it just kept falling and falling until it fell below my $184 entry that July, and after a bad earnings miss that October it crashed into the mid-$70s.

Two things stuck with me. You haven't actually made anything until you sell: a gain on a screen isn't a gain in your pocket. And long-term investing is a completely different game from watching a chart go up and calling yourself a genius.

Unrealized ≠ realized Long-term ≠ short-term
